title: Orchestrate artifact cohorting & driver-pin reconciliation for LTS rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we stabilize multiple LTS tracks and prepare cross-region image rotations, we observe frequent misalignment between container images, published SBOMs, and the pinned CUDA/driver stacks that images expect. This causes two operational risks: 1) runtime incompatibilities when nodes have different driver versions than images assume, and 2) slow, manual rollouts because SREs must reconcile pins and SBOMs by hand.

Goal: Build an orchestrated system that groups images into "cohorts" for rollout (cohorting), canonicalizes and publishes SBOM deltas per-cohort, and automatically reconciles/pins compatible CUDA and driver stacks per LTS channel. The system should enable gated rollouts (canary -> ramp -> full) with automatic compatibility checks and clear audit trails for every rollforward/rollback.

Scope:
- Cohort graph generation for image families (by model runtime, quantization profile, and OS base).
- SBOM canonicalizer that produces compact delta payloads for publish and subscribes to artifact-change events.
- Compatibility matrix service that maps image ABI requirements to driver/CUDA versions; integrates with our kernel-compat database and public vendor matrices.
- A reconciliation orchestrator that proposes driver pins for clusters and emits rollout plans with gates and automated pre-checks.
- CLI/API for release engineers to preview, approve, or abort rollouts; telemetry and dashboards for rollout health.

Non-goal: Replacing OS-level driver management in customer-managed on-prem clusters. This work focuses on Redwood-managed nodes and our dedicated/private offerings where we can control node images and drivers.
acceptance_criteria: Cohorting algorithm produces deterministic cohorts for the current image catalog and can be re-run as new artifacts appear
SBOM canonicalizer publishes delta packages to registry and records a hash+manifest in a release metadata store
Compatibility matrix service returns a stable set of compatible CUDA+driver pins for a given image manifest and LTS channel
Reconciler can generate a staged rollout plan (canary, 3 ramps, full) and apply it to a test cluster automatically
Automated pre-checks block a rollout if a critical incompatibility is detected and record a remediation suggestion
End-to-end smoke tests (runtime-1.19 target) pass on canary cluster with rolled-forward driver pins
Each rollout action has an audit log entry and a link to the SBOM delta used for that cohort
work_items: Design data model for cohort graph and metadata (owner, constraints, stability window)
Implement SBOM canonicalizer + delta generator (OCI registry hooks)
Build compatibility matrix adaptor to vendor/kernel-compat DBs and run offline validation against images from last 6 months
Implement reconciler service that proposes driver pinsets and emits rollout plans
Integrate with console: rollout UI, per-cohort health metrics, and tokenized approval flow
Add pre-check suite: kernel module presence, libc/GLIBC ABI sniff, GPU feature bits
Create e2e tests and a synthetic canary pipeline for runtime-1.19 LTS
Run cross-region dry-run and capture telemetry for incrementally safer ramp rules
Docs: runbook for SRE/release engineers and public-facing changelog entries
